#4266. 10 Pokémon Characters Who Deserved Much More Attention

Laurence Wall is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been writing professionally since 2022 and covering games since 2023. He primarily writes guides and lists, with a focus on indie games, RPGs, ARPGs, Soulslikes, MMOs, card games, boss fights, and detailed tutorials. Before joining DualShockers, Laurence worked as

While Pokémon is best known for the Pokémon themselves, every game brings an eclectic cast of characters we interact with as Pokémon trainers. Whether it’s quirky Gym Leaders, angsty rivals, or just odd folks you meet along the way, your journey is punctuated by these interesting experiences.

This list covers some of the best things players find when taking their time in the Pokémon series.

However, sometimes a character comes along that really makes you pay attention. Maybe it’s the way they look, what they said, or the Pokémon they used, but they stick in your memory somehow. The Pokémon series is full of these characters. More often than not, they appear and disappear as fast as they were introduced, leaving you a little confused about why they didn’t play a bigger role.

Here are a few examples of characters I wish had a bigger role, or were fleshed out a bit more over the course of all nine Generations to date.

Anyone who played the original Diamond and Pearl back in the day will remember Cheryl. She’s the helpful trainer who accompanies you through Eterna Forest, right before the second gym. You might think she doesn’t have much of a role, since all she does is heal your Pokémon with her Chansey and then wander off, yet she seems to recur throughout the franchise.

Cheryl reappears later in the Battleground, a place generally reserved for powerful trainers, with a team of Pokémon with crazy-high HP stats, and also in the Battle Tower. She also appears in Pokémon Generations, getting lost in The Old Chateau, and seems to have a relative in Hisui called Sabi.

It’s a shame we never got to see a bit more from Cheryl in the story, or even in something like Pokémon Contests!

Mohn has always been a pretty interesting character in Pokémon Sun and Moon. You’ll originally meet him when you’re introduced to the Poke Pelago; however, you might notice he looks a little familiar.

Long story short, Mohn was originally a researcher at the Aether Foundation and Lusamine's husband. However, when we meet him, he’s unfortunately lost his memory. It’s rumoured that when researching the Ultra Wormholes, he fell into one and developed amnesia, but this topic isn’t really explored much.

I would have loved a bit more backstory about Mohn, his relationship with his family and just what happened to him when travelling through Ultra Space. However, we may never know.

Marley, like Cheryl, is a Generation 4 character we meet while exploring a certain area of the game. This area is an offshoot of Victory Road and can only be explored in the Post-Game.

Marley doesn’t like to talk much and seems very caring. As such, while she does have an Arcanine, it’s also equipped with Helping Hand to assist you in battle. Like Cheryl, she can also be found in the Battleground and the Battle Tower, and she specialises in high-speed Pokémon.

The thing is, Marley obviously has a connection to Shaymin, which the game doesn’t really develop much. She helps us reach Seabreak Path and can even be found there again if you bring Oak’s Letter. On top of this, in Pokémon Masters, she even has a Shaymin! Is she just an interested trainer, or is there more to it?

Malva is the Fire-type Elite Four member of the Kalos region. Most Elite Four members don’t have much to offer, aside from an interesting design. However, Malva is hiding something far more sinister beneath the surface.

From Ultra Necrozma’s stat boosts to Volo’s grueling final battle, these Pokémon encounters bend the rules to deliver memorable challenges.

See, Malva is actually part of the heinous Team Flare, which you work to dismantle throughout the game. We learn later, in Legends Z-A, that Malva was there when they captured the legendary Pokémon Yveltal and helped take it down.

This is why she seems so prickly towards you when you face her in the Pokémon League. I would have liked to see a bit more of Malva and learn more about her involvement with Team Flare. The Flare storyline always seemed a bit weak after all.

Thankfully, Malva seems to learn her lesson and helps us with Dr Xerosic in the X and Y postgame, somewhat redeeming herself.

Benga is a really odd character. He’s obviously the Grandson of the Champion, Alder; that’s pretty obvious from his radical hairstyle. However, it’s never explained how Benga got so powerful. More so than his Grandfather, the Champion, might I repeat!

Benga is the final boss of the White Treehollow in White 2 or the Black Tower in Black 2. As such, he has an absolutely ludicrous team of Latios/Latias, Garchomp/Dragonite, and a Volcarona. While the Volcarona is obviously a nod to Alder, how on earth did this little kid get his hands on a pair of legendaries?

Once you’ve defeated him, you can head back to Floccesy Town, where Benga will offer you either a Shiny Gible or a Shiny Dratini. Now he seems to have shiny Pokémon to offer you, but how did he get these? This kid is a real mystery.

Starting in Generation 5, you can find Ingo in the Battle Subway, where he serves as a main boss alongside his brother Emmet. And for a long time, that’s where he stayed. A fairly obscure, relatively uninteresting character who didn’t draw much attention.

However, you might be surprised to come across Ingo in Hisui, in Pokémon Legends: Arceus. And no, this isn’t some ancient relative like most other Sinnoh trainers; this really is Ingo, having travelled through time and lost a good chunk of his memories. But why him, and not a Sinnoh character?

Thankfully, Ingo gets a happy ending, as we learn in Legends Z-A that he eventually returned to Unova and reunited with his brother Emmet. Turns out even the most unassuming trainer can have their secrets!

And speaking of people being zapped across Space and Time, here we have Anabel. We were originally introduced to Anabel in Pokémon Emerald, where she served as a Frontier Brain, one of the most powerful and difficult trainers in the entire series.

After defeating the Elite Four, these are the Pokémon Games Where the Post-Game Feels Like a Whole New Adventure.

However, fast-forward to Pokémon Sun and Moon, and we meet Anabel again; like Ingo, she’s been mysteriously transported to Alola, this time through an Ultra Wormhole rather than by Arceus. Now she’s part of the International Police, and as part of the UB task force, she’s there to round up the rabid Ultra Beasts rampaging across the region.

We know Anabel is a strong trainer, before and after the incident, but how did she enter the Ultra Wormhole in the first place? Was she chosen? Or was it just random chance? We never really get an answer here. It would have been nice to get a little more backstory into what happened in Hoenn.

Zinnia appears only in the Generation 3 remakes, Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire. During the adventure, you run into her masquerading as part of the evil team, but you soon learn she’s actually part of an ancient group trying to summon Rayquaza.

She plays a larger role in the Delta Episode; however, all her efforts are for nothing, as the main character ends up Mega Evolving Rayquaza and stopping the Meteor.

Zinnia has a fantastic, interesting design, and the bits and pieces we get of her backstory make it seem like she’ll play a bigger role in the story. She seems to know so much more than we do, especially about the Pokémon Multiverse, but again, we never fully explore her story. At least we still have that incredible battle theme!

If you’ve played Pokémon Colosseum or XD, you’ll have fond memories of this utterly bizarre trainer. Miror B is a funky villain and one of the four admins of Team Cipher. However, you’ll quickly notice that while he might be on the bad side, his real passion is actually dancing!

And not only does he like to bust a move, but his Pokémon do too! And, I have to admit, he’s got one of the best battle songs in the entire Pokémon series! The cool thing about Miror B is that, once defeated, he actually leaves Team Cipher in order to set up his own group, whom you meet in the sequel. He might never quite renounce his wicked ways, but for entertainment, you don’t get much better than this.

It’s certainly a shame we never got to see more of Miror B, as Game Freak seems determined to ignore Genius Sonority’s twin masterpieces.

Yep, this is one for the OGs. I remember back in Primary school, when rumours of Mew being under the truck were still floating around, there was another rumour about the dark side of the kind and generous Mr. Fuji.

The thing is, this one actually holds water, unlike the Mew story. You first find Mr. Fuji in Lavender Town, looking after orphaned Pokémon, and defending the Marowak from Team Rocket in Pokémon Tower. We later learn that Mr. Fuji and Blaine were good friends, and that they both worked on a project in the burned-down Pokémon Mansion over on Cinnabar.

Of course, the theory is that Mr. Fuji was one of the scientists who created Mewtwo through genetic experimentation on Mew. He was so traumatised by his creation that he vowed never to hurt a Pokémon again, and moved to Lavender Town to atone for his misdeeds.

This theory is reflected in the Pokémon Origins series and in Dr. Fuji in Mewtwo Strikes Back. We also know Mr. Fuji travelled to Faraway Island and left a note for the trainer before they find Mew. Was this the original Mew used to create Mewtwo?

However, I'm fairly certain we never actually got the official answer to this theory in the mainline games. For now, we’ll have to rely on theories to sate our appetite for Pokémon lore! Maybe one day we’ll know for sure?

From NPC placements to move typings, these are the Pokémon FireRed & LeafGreen Changes That Quietly Improved the Original Games.

#4264. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

#4261. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4260. 10 Metroidvanias With the Most Nominations at The Game Awards

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

Although Metroidvanias have been largely dominated by indie games since video game award ceremonies became commonplace, this hasn't diminished their presence at the industry's most important gala events.

Today, the indie ecosystem is just as capable as AAA titles of delivering masterpieces, which has led to them gaining a more prominent role whenever we gather to review each year's best releases.

Certainly, it's not as prominent a genre as RPGs or pure action-adventure games, but it has still had enough presence to demonstrate that it's a variant that has nothing to envy in the legitimacy of others.

Therefore, clarifying beforehand that several titles will be omitted for sharing the last spot with only one nomination, prioritizing instead those that were most relevant, these are the ten Metroidvanias with the most nominations at The Game Awards.

Along with another title that will be featured later, Axiom Verge marks the first year a Metroidvania earned a nomination; in this case, for Best Independent Game of 2015.

Although it had to contend with notable releases like the global phenomenon Rocket League and the indie gem Undertale, Tom Happ secured his place in the genre's history thanks to his magnificent science fiction journey.

In an era when Metroidvanias hadn't yet established themselves as a major force, this solo developer created such a captivating title that, to this day, it still has few direct competitors in its craftsmanship, as it is truly unique.

Nothing would please me more today than an Axiom Verge 3, so this is a fitting opportunity to recall the historic feat achieved by the first entry and ask Happ to consider repeating that glory soon.

As a living legend of contemporary Metroidvanias, single-handedly setting the course for the genre in the decade following its release, Hollow Knight couldn't be left off this list.

However, contrary to what one might think today, Team Cherry's creation only received a nomination for Best Indie Debut in 2017, which it lost to a colossus that, upon its release, made a greater impact: Cuphead.

Even so, time would gradually vindicate this masterpiece, whose aura would extend to all subsequent developments, rewriting history in the memories of many who recall, albeit mistakenly, that it was nominated in more categories.

The power of hindsight is undeniable when the subject is a title with Hollow Knight's legacy, which also highlights how indie games, over the years, have become increasingly respected and taken seriously in these spaces.

From indies to multiplayers, these ten video games that defined the 2010s shaped the industry as we know it today.

Leaving aside the inevitable debate about Dead Cells as a Metroidvania, Motion Twin made history by being one of the first games in the genre to receive multiple nominations at The Game Awards.

Historically, this fusion of the genre with the roguelike philosophy earned the second Metroidvania award in the event's history by winning Best Action Game in 2018, though it lost the Best Independent Game category to the acclaimed Celeste.

In the category it won, it faced stiff competition from titanic blockbusters like Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Destiny 2: Forsaken, and Far Cry 5, though this didn't prevent what would eventually become one of the best-selling indie games of all time from taking home the prize.

The recognition is, of course, more than deserved, given that few titles in the last decade are capable of generating the excitement and addictiveness that Dead Cells produces, so no matter how many AAA games they had put against it, it would have won anyway.

That high-caliber developers like Ubisoft are investing in the genre to revitalize their longest-running franchises is a relatively new trend, yet it yielded definitive results with Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown.

The presence of a game in the genre with such a strong production value allowed it to win an unprecedented honor for Metroidvanias, the Innovation in Accessibility Award in 2024, although it lost the Best Action-Adventure Game category to Astro Bot.

Regardless, it was the first medal at The Game Awards that the French developer received after winning Best Sim/Strategy Game with Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope in 2022, making its impact in terms of recognition significant.

Furthermore, it's an extraordinary video game with a superb level of polish and freshness, so hopefully Ubisoft will recognize this trend and begin to replicate what they did with Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown with several of their most forgotten and missed IPs.

2024 was a fertile year for indie games, and although it didn't win either of the categories it was nominated for—because Balatro is larger than life—Animal Well remains in the collective imagination as an unparalleled masterpiece.

As part of the nominees for Best Independent Game and Best Indie Debut in 2024, Billy Basso stood tall with his iconic solo project against giants of the indie ecosystem like Devolver Digital, Kepler Interactive, and Annapurna Interactive without hesitation.

Basso picks up the mantle from Happ and doubles Axiom Verge's achievement almost a decade later, doing so with a game that defies Metroidvania conventions and replaces all combat with countless intricate yet wonderful puzzles that completely immerse you in the adventure.

Two years later, Animal Well remains one of my most cherished memories of the entire decade, and I think it will likely stay there for... a lifetime.

From the hops and dashes in Hollow Knight to the integral platforming of Pseudoregalia, these are 10 Metroidvanias with satisfying platforming.

The first of this list's five Metroidvanias to be nominated for three or more awards is none other than Tunic, the indie gem that swept through audiences and critics alike in 2022, establishing itself among the genre's most outstanding representatives this generation.

Unfortunately, its nominations for Best Independent Game, Best Action-Adventure Game, and Best Indie Debut in 2022 didn't result in any badges, as it was up against GOTY contenders like Stray and God of War: Ragnarök, though this only underscores its impressive quality.

That essence reminiscent of The Legend of Zelda didn't go unnoticed, and it underpinned the structure of one of recent years' most exciting and intriguing adventures, particularly because of its decision not to hold your hand and instead rely on your ability to find your way through combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving.

The fact that Tunic is the first video game from its developers is absolutely incredible, and that under said conditions it achieved three nominations on the most anticipated night in the video game industry is quite high recognition.

As one of the most exquisite audiovisual expressions the genre has witnessed since its inception, Ori and the Will of the Wisps was an inevitable presence on any list of this caliber.

Moon Studios' sequel was among the nominees for Best Art Direction, Best Music, and Best Action-Adventure Game in 2020, though unfortunately, it had to compete against absolute generational masterpieces like Ghost of Tsushima, Final Fantasy VII Remake, and The Last of Us Part II.

However, as with Tunic, Ori and the Will of the Wisps being considered alongside numerous video games that have defined the decade is one of the greatest displays of Metroidvania greatness on the big stage.

It's no wonder the title consistently appears on lists of the best of its kind, and one that would have completely swept its categories had it been nominated in years less dominated by modern classics.

Metroid Dread made history as the first Metroidvania to be nominated for Game of the Year in 2021, and for many it was the true winner of the category that, ultimately, went to It Takes Two.

Regardless of the debate, MercurySteam solidified its relationship with Nintendo by bringing Samus Aran back to 2D, reinforcing it as the natural home of the iconic bounty hunter by delivering a near-perfect creation.

It was also nominated for Best Action-Adventure Game, which it won, and for Players’ Voice, which it lost, thus becoming the second game in the genre to win a category after Dead Cells, despite probably deserving more.

The mother of all the entries on this list is an inseparable part of its history, and although perhaps not to the fullest extent, its participation in The Game Awards is a recognition of that legacy.

From the ever-challenging Celeste to some surprisingly difficult gems, these are the 10 Hardest Indie Games To 100% Complete.

With four nominations and one victory, Ori and the Blind Forest is pure Metroidvania history, bursting onto the scene at the interactive industry's most prestigious awards ceremony as the genre's first appearance (alongside Axiom Verge).

Developed by a much smaller team than when they collaborated with Microsoft on the sequel, and as a less experienced studio within a still largely unexplored genre, the project was nominated for Best Independent Game, Best Art Direction, Best Score, and Best Action-Adventure in 2015.

Of all the nominations, it took home the award for its visual direction, beating out Bloodborne, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Metal Gear Solid 5: The Phantom Pain, one of the biggest surprises the ceremony has ever seen.

While this is a more common and normal occurrence these days, the fact that Ori and the Blind Forest achieved such a strong presence, and even managed to win an award among a couple of candidates for best game of all time, is simply beyond belief.

What I consider the best Metroidvania of all time is also the most recognized game in the genre at The Game Awards, leaving Hollow Knight: Silksong with the most nominations at six, though it only managed one win.

Game of the Year, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Independent Game, Players’ Voice, and Best Action-Adventure Game were the categories in which Team Cherry's unimaginable sequel was nominated, ultimately taking home the last one.

Like Ori and the Blind Forest, Hornet had to overcome giants such as Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, Ghost of Yotei, and Split Fiction to win the award, a remarkable achievement considering the team is still just three people.

In the categories it didn't win, it was surpassed by the now-legendary Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, which took home four of the six awards in which it shared nominations, and Wuthering Waves, which won the user vote.

In any case, Hollow Knight: Silksong is the Metroidvania with the most nominations at The Game Awards, and it's tough to imagine when we'll see another title that can match such a record.

From classics like Teslagrad to modern gems like Blasphemous, these are ten Metroidvania franchises that should come back in 2027.

What happens if you run out of dice in Monopoly Go? Of course, the game will also bombard you with offers to buy more if that's something you're into.  Should I save my dice on Monopoly Go? Generally speaking, you don't want to use all of your dice rolls without good reason. While it's tempting to empty them all out at once, you're often better off saving them for the right moment, such as for High Roller, Golden Blitz or Partner Events. Doing so will allow you to progress further in those rather than struggling to get anywhere. Of course, it's all up to you. #4257. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4256. Best Netflix games available right now - From Into the Breach to Red Dead Redemption

Netflix isn't just a place to watch movies and TV episodes - it's also a great place for gamers to discover new forms of entertainment, with a large library of games from many different developers and genres.

There are numerous hours of fun to be had on Netflix for gamers, from action to puzzle games. On the next pages, you can find a list we compiled after carefully considering all the available games and narrowing them down to give you the top 10 best Netflix games at the moment. How to find and install Netflix Games If you don't have it already, go ahead and download the Netflix app on your device. Keep in mind that you need to have an active Netflix subscription for this.

Now, let's get on with the list of best Netflix games at the moment.

If you don't know anything about the Football Manager franchise, you must be either living under a rock or you just don't like football. But if you do like football and simulation games, then this is a no-brainer.

Become a club manager and take everything under your control, from tactics and transfers to team talks, scouting, and pretty much anything else that you can imagine.

You can start your career at any club in the world, as it supports every league and has real players. As I said, this game is a must if you are looking for a football simulation experience.

Download now! Football Manager 26 Mobile

You already know about Bloons TD 6 from our previous articles, such as Bloons TD 6 tier list and best towers to carry your rounds. In this Netflix game, you benefit from hundreds of configurations and upgrades, so feel free to read all the guides we've created to help you on that journey.

Aside from that, what you need to know about this game is that it's wild. You have a tower defence type of game where things get increasingly more difficult. Towards the last levels, some players even reported crashes because of how crazy the battles turned out.

It's one of the most fun and entertaining tower defence games out there, and easily one of the best games Netflix has to offer.

Oxenfree is a story-driven adventure game with elements of mystery and suspense, sprinkled with paranormal elements.

The story follows a group of teenagers as they face the repercussions of opening a ghostly portal on an abandoned island, while out partying one night. It's also got a smart chat system that lets players have a major impact on the tale's action and conclusion.

New graphics, a remixed soundtrack, a new epilogue, mysteries, and branching story paths can all be found in Oxenfree: Netflix Edition, which was published on September 24th, 2022. If you are interested in this title, here's a link to our full review of Oxenfree, where we get into specifics.

Before Your Eyes is a game with a major focus on storytelling and beauty. The actual story is a little dark at its core, but the way it is presented is far from it.

It gives players the opportunity to immerse themselves in an individual's life, as they journey across the River Styx and into the afterlife. That is as dark as it appears, but it has its beauty.

Before Your Eyes has innovative gameplay with real-time tracking of the player's eye movements and blinking to make choices that impact the outcome of the story. It's not something we typically see in your run-of-the-mill mobile game.

Krispee Street is an adorably designed hidden object game that is exclusively accessible to Netflix members. This title draws inspiration from a well-known webcomic, and its graphics don't shy away from showing that. It's really well done.

As a player, you'll have to figure out puzzles and discover well-hidden objects, and while it might sound like a piece of cake at first, it really isn't. Oh, and it also has a certain narrative that it manages to tell between the puzzles and hidden object games. It's really good, and a nice break from the classical, realistic hidden object game we're used to.

As a kid, you've probably dreamed of defending the Earth from various calamities or invasions and being a hero in the end. Well, Into the Breach will make your childhood dream finally come true. You're the last line of defence against the overgrown bug-like aliens that can crush a building without much effort. However, humanity has advanced, and we have huge mechs and other weapons of destruction because we humans are great at finding the best way to kill each other.

Fighting is done on an 8x8 grid that's similar to chess, with turn-based combat. As terrain can shift and create huge holes in the ground, it can be tricky to avoid them while facing aliens. Therefore, careful planning is essential to win every round, no matter what the end goal is. That's the only way to turn terrain shifts to your advantage, as gravity works on your adversaries as well.

Storyteller is a hit game unlike any other. It starts off pretty slow, with just a couple of prompts, but soon enough you will find yourself in a story unlike any other. The game is available on Steam as well, which is where it was first popularised.

The best part about Storyteller is not the fact that it's sort of a build-your-own-story kind of game, but rather its unique take on it. You will be in charge of making a plot for each prompt you're given, and sometimes these plots have a twist. Literally. It's one of the best Netflix games ever released, and you shouldn't skip it.

Red Dead Redemption likely needs no introduction, though we should take a moment to appreciate how far mobile has come before we get to that. The fact that we can now carry an incredibly complex and detailed open-world shooter like this in our pockets shows the leaps in technology since the game first released way back in 2010.

If you're somehow unfamiliar, it takes place in the Wild West and follows John Marston as he hunts down the surviving members of his old gang. Why? The federal government has taken his family and won't give them back until the job is done. Yeah, it's pretty heavy stuff and is a wonderfully told story. In some ways, I'd argue, it's better than its successor, Red Dead 2. I appreciate that’s a contentious statement, of course.

But it's not all gloomy stuff. Thanks to the open-world nature of it all, there's plenty of twisted fun to be had with tying people to train tracks and waiting for the next locomotive to roll through. Or if you don’t want to act like a Looney Tunes villain, you can swagger into a saloon, find a comfortable corner, and play poker for hours instead. It’s good fun either way.

Download now! Red Dead Redemption NETFLIX

Death might not be the happiest topic in the world, but that doesn't mean it can't provide some level of catharsis when handled well. Spiritfarer takes this complex life event and somehow manages to turn it into a cosy management RPG.

You play as a ferrymaster tasked with guiding the recently passed to the afterlife. It's not a simple case of starting the engines and sailing across to the other side, though. The spirits you encounter are somewhat restless, and you'll need to care for them as they make their final voyage. That means getting to know them and their needs, which makes for an incredibly emotional final goodbye. Still, it's that bittersweet variety of sadness where you'll be pleased you took the plunge.

Aside from chatting to Spiritfarer's lovable cast, you'll also busy yourself with fishing, crafting, mining, farming, and all manner of other things. Just because your destination is a fairly morbid one, it doesn't mean that everyday tasks can fall by the wayside, you see. They're still important and in many ways key to the relaxing vibe Spiritfarer offers.

I've had fairly mixed opinions about Black Mirror ever since it jumped to Netflix. Though there have been plenty of good episodes since that move (Hi, San Junipero), I mostly find the quality has dipped (What was that awful werewolf episode all about?). However, Season 6's Plaything does stand out as one of the better offerings from the later series.

Now, that could simply be because my opinion is swayed by the video game stuff or the fantastic performance from Peter Capaldi (The best Doctor Who since the show's revival. Sorry, David). But either way, the fictional video game featured in it isn't actually fictional. Sort of. That's right, you can actually play Thronglets! It's just these little critters don't plan to kill us all... I think.

Inspired by Black Mirror mastermind Charlie Brooker's obsession with keeping a Tamagotchi alive in his youth, Thronglets is a virtual pet sim that tasks you with helping the Throng thrive. They'll hatch from eggs before relying on you for food and entertainment. Do all those things, and you'll have an adorable little army (?). Just don't set them all on fire, alright? They don't take too kindly to that.

#4255. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

Invictus Gaming knocked out fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening quarter-final of Worlds 2026 in Allen, Texas. The result guarantees China a semi-final place after the LPL's 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage.

Invictus Gaming are through to the last four of Worlds 2026. They beat fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening match of the Knockout Stage. The series was played at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas, on 3 November (US time).

The win guarantees China a semi-final place. That matters after the LPL’s 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage. IG now meet either Gen.G or LYON. Gen.G beat IG 1-0 in the Swiss Stage and finished it with a perfect 3-0 record.

TES played the event without ZUIAN. On 6 October the club announced that Bai ‘369’ Jia-Hao would move into the starting line-up because of visa problems affecting ZUIAN.

The stand-in still made his mark. IG won Game 1 after building a gold lead of more than 10,000. TES levelled in Game 2 when 369, on Renekton, killed JiaQi and TheShy on his own late in the game. IG then took the next two games to close out the series.

Every Knockout Stage match is a single-elimination best-of-five played with Fearless Draft. The two sides knew each other well. They met twice in best-of-five series in September. IG won 3-2 in the LPL Split 3 playoffs on 5 September. TES won 3-1 in the LPL Regional Finals on 17 September.

The prize money gap is now fixed. Worlds 2026 has a total prize pool of US$5,000,000, with US$1,000,000 for the winner. Each losing semi-finalist receives US$400,000, so IG are guaranteed at least that sum.

IG’s run began with a mid-season rescue. The team started LPL Split 3 in the Nirvana Group. The club then asked TheShy and Rookie, who were both on a break, to come back. The pair helped the side qualify for Worlds. Both won the 2018 world title with IG.

TheShy said he had promised IG’s CEO he would help if asked. “I came back to keep my word,” he said after the series.

#4252. SoundMagic E11C review - "Affordable and well designed"

SoundMagic is known for its affordable range of in-ear headphones, which have put it on the map, especially as people turn to more wired earbuds for their devices. This is a trend that seemed to have started with people in Hollywood, but has continued to be seen making a comeback.

The SoundMagic E11C earbuds have a silver wire coated in plastic, making them feel very durable. There's a volume control right by the side of your face and a quick mute when using the microphone that's built in. The earbuds themselves are also made of aluminium, with three different tip sizes that you can easily pop on and off to wear them. These tips allow you to choose one that blocks out outside sound, isolating noise, so that you have a better experience.

This is a 3.5mm headphone cable connection, so you will need to have a dongle to connect them to USB-C or Apple devices, but that's pretty standard these days! I found the sound quality to be very good, especially for the price. It was easy to plug them in - no Bluetooth connection to pair them up.

The SoundMagic E11c have a sensitivity rating of 112dB, which means that you can increase the volume quite a bit. If you listen to music or games at the average listening volume, it will actually use less of your device's power, which is pretty cool.

The SoundMagic E11C comes with a carrying case, where you can put your various ear tips and keep your wires from getting tangled into the rest of your belongings when placed into your bag. It's a hard case, so it won't get crushed either.

Overall, it's a great pair of budget earbuds that feel well-made and work great for those who travel or want a pair of earbuds that don't require charging - as long as you have the right dongle for your device!

#4250. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. #4247. Best racing games for Android

A list of the finest racing games that you can play on Android in 2026 to satisfy that need for speed.

Remember when you had to pump a bunch of coins into a giant arcade cabinet if you wanted to play the latest and greatest titles? Now all you need is an Android phone, and it doesn't even have to be an expensive one.

Modern phones are a marvel, and they offer access to a vast and eclectic roster of racing and driving titles.

Why do we distinguish between racing and driving? It's simple, really - not all titles in which you control a vehicle are about dashing to the finish line. There's just way more variety out there these days.

Yes, you still get your arcade games on the Google Play Store. But there are also karts, simulators, management games, and weird little genre mash-ups that don't involve racing at all.

Comfortably the finest pure racing experience, GRID Autosport offers a startlingly faithful premium console experience with some truly stunning 3D graphics. It feels as good as it would on a console, and the touch controls are nothing short of amazing.

So, what differentiates GRID from the rest on this list? Besides the exceptional gameplay and realistic physics, it has a unique feature. You can turn back time! It's important because a crash here can leave your car broken, so you can reverse time for a few seconds and continue driving without making the same mistake again, hopefully. Of course, it has a limited number of uses; otherwise, it would just be plain old cheating.

Racing doesn't have to be constrained to the tarmac. Indeed, Reckless Racing 3 revels in the slidey delights that come from removing friction from the equation. It's a stunning title that prides itself on several features, including the smooth controls and spot-on genre touches.

You will find over twenty awesome vehicles, more than thirty unique routes, and fantastic modes, such as arcade, career, and others. Physics and gravity are purely optional when it comes to Asphalt 9, a riotously OTT arcade game that can't help but make you smile. It's easy peasy to get into, and boy, does it look pretty. It's the successor to one of the best racing games for Android of all time - Asphalt 8!

A brilliantly balanced title that combines authentic muck-specked simulation with intuitive arcade racing. Nintendo's signature kart racer screeches onto mobile. While it's far from perfect, and perhaps a little too casual and 'freemium' for Nintendo die-hards, there's no doubt that its one-finger controls still feel like Mario Kart. And yes, it's a serious racer even though it looks cartoonish.

If you're interested already, our tier list of the best Mario Kart karts and best drivers in Mario Kart Tour will both come in handy.
